question: Which canonical mappings preserve document meaning through Markdown parse/serialize, and where must loss be explicit?
trigger: Explicit user request: $best-api-review audit markdown, after import/export conversion and paste-diagnostic closure.
requirements: Audit all ten declared contract/consumer units; retain separate review, adoption and proof states.
Preserve representable Markdown meaning; diagnose intentional or unsupported loss and obey the existing reject/allow policy.
Keep literal code unchanged and ensure inline results contain inline content; incomplete-input recovery cannot silently omit source.
Make MDAST/MDX selector inference agree with actual dispatch and distinguish programmer/configuration failures from content rejection.
Keep detached conversion, installed editor convenience, feature-owned mappings and exact-editor versus broad standalone typing where current jobs justify them.
Challenge deletion of duplicated paths and unconsumed public options without compatibility aliases on next.
Leave AI policy, incremental streaming performance, generic list topology, HTML sanitizer and external-text synchronization in their separate scopes.
Assessment and history updates only; no product implementation, downstream execution plan or publication.
evidenceReuse: Reconciled recovered July colocation/package-cut outcomes, September conversion naming/carrier/type and diagnostic executions, the document-first export plan, and list/streaming history. Re-read current owners and real import/export, server, Copilot, AIChat, schema-descriptor and conversion/streaming demo consumers. Two bounded native agents inspected mapping declarations and serialization; main audited parse/runtime/options/docs. Historical tests are not promoted to current proof. Fresh bounded existing tests and disposable probes establish specific counterexamples only.
summary: Pursue a smaller and correct Markdown conversion owner. Delete whole-source HTML-to-JSX rewriting, destructive inline stripping, and unused withBlockId transport plus its alternate list serializer. Keep parse/serialize names, document/slice/inline jobs, broad standalone Value, exact-editor methods, core authoring types, optional runtime and feature-owned mappings. Repair MDAST/MDX selector inference, programmer-error ownership, inline admission, incomplete recovery, document-wide references, footnote blocks, mark merging, list-filter flushing, null overrides and loss accounting for properties/open roots. Ten of ten audit units reviewed (nine Pursue, one Stop/retain); all have dispositions. No universal codec, extra reference registry, generic property-accounting framework or Plite Markdown layer is justified.

alternatives: Configure withoutMdx at callers: Stop; callers still need MDX, and owner-level source corruption, inline loss and duplicated policies remain.
Patch regexes and retain withBlockId's alternate list serializer: Stop; regexes cannot establish code context and the unused transport retains a separate incorrect algorithm.
Cut parseInline: Stop; Copilot has a current inline insertion job. Validate its promised carrier and reject or diagnose block content.
Only editor APIs or only standalone functions: Stop; detached/server conversion and installed configuration are distinct jobs. Retain the private shared implementation.
Centralize mappings or move Markdown into core/Plite: Stop; feature colocation preserves optional dependencies and schema roles already supply substrate laws.
Introduce a universal codec/compiler/session, public reference registry or generic consumed-property framework: Stop; no independent current job justifies those nouns.

Keep format ownership, delete unsafe preprocessing and block-ID transport, and repair typed mappings plus conversion-local references/loss accounting: Pursue; it removes observed corruption and duplicate algorithms without a new public subsystem.

Collapse allowedNodes/disallowedNodes through existing allowNode: compare during Task design against the declarative subset job; do not add another filter API. Keep plainMarks' independently exercised text-preserving job.
proofLimits: Read-only product audit; only disposable proof and review metadata changed. Main parser probes: 1 passing control, 7 failing behavior assertions. Fresh existing runs: MarkdownPlugin 30/30, sync/GFM 8/8, mapping/features 30/30 across six files, serializers 59/59 across five files; GFM overlaps runs, so not a unique total. Serializer observation probe captures 22 outcomes and passes only an observation-count assertion. Mapping probes ran in memory; their returned commands/results are preserved in a receipt. Earlier serializer fixture/setup failures are excluded. Ten selected units and 44 feature mappings inspected; no exhaustive arbitrary-property/input corpus, new implementation, full typecheck/package run, browser/native clipboard, external viewer, comparative performance proof or external block-ID consumer inventory. Limits remain postparse for nodes/depth. Historical receipts keep their own proof limits.
